BirosieeY ay THE
UNITED STA OF AMERICA

JUN 24 1938

“e Executive Order

FurRTHER EXEMPTION OF JoHN H. Tuomas From CoMPULSORY
RETIREMENT FOR AGE

WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that John H. Thomas,
Assistant Solicitor and member of the Board of Appeals, Department of the Interior,
who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period one year ending
September 30, 1938, by Executive Order No. 7637 of June 19, 1937, be further
exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S. C., title 5, sec. 715a),
I hereby further exempt the said John H. Thomas from compulsory retirement for
age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
Tue Wuirte Hovss,
June 16, 1938.

[No. 7912]

U.S. GOVERNNENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1938

Thomas from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The recital identifies John H. Thomas as a person who had been exempted for a period one year ending September 30, 1938, by Executive Order No. 7637 of June 19, 1937; that earlier exemption is a separate instrument, and nothing in it affects when this one ends. The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362896, Common Crawl capture 2024-12-02T23:08:22Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7912, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on September 30, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The OFR catalog search and the held-text name search both report zero hits for this order, so no revoking, superseding or extending instrument is recorded in the packet.
